title: How to Keep a Clear Record of Money You Lend and Borrow
excerpt: Track peer loans, Qarz-e-Hasana, installment repayments, and outstanding balances with clear digital records.
introduction: In Pakistan, informal peer-to-peer lending among family, friends, and colleagues is culturally common. Keeping a clear written record protects both parties and eliminates misunderstandings. This educational guide covers informal bookkeeping and mutual accountability in Pakistani Rupees (PKR), not commercial banking credit or legal advice.
author: HisabKi Kitab Editorial Team

blocks.text: Informal peer loans and mutual aid (Qarz-e-Hasana) often begin with verbal promises or casual text messages. When repayments occur in small, irregular installments over several months, memories naturally diverge about how much was originally lent, what has been repaid, and what balance remains.

A reliable personal debt ledger (Digital Khata) requires five core fields for every transaction: (1) date, (2) principal amount, (3) parties involved, (4) agreed repayment milestones, and (5) a running updated balance. Informal personal loans are zero-interest agreements where the borrower repays only the exact principal received. Both parties should have access to the same ledger to maintain complete mutual confidence.

Tariq extends an interest-free personal loan of PKR 50,000 to his colleague Usman on 1 August for emergency vehicle repairs. They agree on a 3-month milestone schedule. Usman makes partial repayments in September and October before clearing the final balance in November.

blocks.caption: Multi-installment personal debt ledger in Pakistani Rupees (PKR)

blocks.text: Remaining Balance = Original Loan Principal − Sum of Confirmed Partial Payments. PKR 50,000 Principal − (PKR 15,000 + PKR 15,000 + PKR 20,000) = PKR 0 remaining balance.

items: Confirm loan expectations in writing upfront: agree on repayment dates, partial installment amounts, and payment methods.
Always use traceable digital payment channels (Raast ID or online banking transfer) with a clear note (e.g., 'Loan installment').
Log every repayment immediately upon receipt, noting the date, amount, and updated balance.
Share an updated balance confirmation with the other person after every installment.
If unexpected circumstances delay a payment, communicate proactively with a realistic revised timeline before the due date passes.
Counting a promised repayment as received before cleared funds appear in your account.
Deducting casual shared expenses (like paying for lunch) from a loan balance without recording it in the ledger.
Lending money that you will need for your own urgent living costs or rent within the next 30 to 60 days.
Feeling embarrassed about requesting a written record—transparency demonstrates professionalism and protects both individuals.

blocks.text: When reminding a friend or relative about an upcoming due date, keep the message factual and polite. A simple note such as 'Hi Usman, just confirming our record shows the second installment of PKR 15,000 is due on 5 October' removes emotional friction and maintains goodwill.

Good financial bookkeeping does not reflect distrust; it protects personal relationships. By keeping an objective, transparent record of money lent and borrowed, you safeguard your peace of mind and ensure mutual respect.

faqs.question: How can I track money lent to friends and family without causing awkwardness? (Udhar ka hisab kaise rakhein?)
faqs.answer: Position record-keeping as mutual bookkeeping rather than suspicion. Send a friendly digital message confirming the date, principal amount, and agreed repayment milestones so both parties have an identical point of reference.

faqs.question: What information should be recorded for every loan repayment?
faqs.answer: Record the payment date, transfer reference or receipt, amount paid, and the new updated outstanding balance. Both parties should verify the updated figure.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Qarz-e-Hasana and commercial debt?
faqs.answer: Qarz-e-Hasana is an interest-free personal loan extended out of goodwill where the borrower repays only the exact principal amount without interest charges, markups, or commercial penalties.
